instructions.question: What sentiment does this Albanian Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Negative needs a strong negative emotion: horror or despair words, fed-up complaints, insults or curses, saying the institute lies or inflates the numbers (including jokes like 'admin, stop your hand'), or anger at the measures or government. Neutral is calm, reasoned or playful: questions, data requests, calculations, mild worry, doubting the virus itself, arguments about testing or citizens' behaviour without insults, and jokes about towns, friends or lab staff. Positive covers praise, thanks, blessings, relief or good news about recoveries, and hopeful encouragement. Town pride and off-topic congratulations are neutral.

neutral.what: Calm, playful or reasoned comments: questions, data requests, calculations, mild worry, speculation about undercounting or the virus, advice, criticism of citizens without insults, teasing friends, jokes about lab staff, tags.
examples: Pse ka Mitrovica Verit nuk po jepni Rezultate hiq !? (Why aren't you giving any results for North Mitrovica!?)
Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit (The lab guy got up early today)
Nese dikush beson qe egziston babadimeri le tbeson edhe covid-19 (If someone believes Santa Claus exists, let them believe in COVID-19 too)
neutral.cues: hahaha, tagged names, pse (why), a ka (is there), duhet (should), hajde ma gjall (come on, livelier), sa keq (how bad), alarm, kuku (oh dear), kampion (champion), numbers
neutral.not_for: Comments with horror words, insults, curses, or claims the institute lies or inflates numbers are negative.

positive.what: Praise, thanks, blessings, relief that cases are falling, good news about recoveries, hopeful encouraging appeals.
examples: Asllan A Haxholli A ka lajm mat mir, 35 t'sherum (Is there better news, 35 recovered)
Shyqyr qeky nxeht e nali pak viusin se ke tu na shkatrru a (Thank God this heat has slowed the virus a bit, it was ruining us)
Perhajr edhe Juve (Blessings to you too)
positive.cues: bravo, ju lumtë (well done), faleminderit (thank you), shyqyr (thank God), lajm i mirë (good news), mir asht (it's good), t'sherum (recovered), shendet (health), mashallah, perhajr (congratulations/blessings)
positive.not_for: Sarcastic praise is negative. 'Prishtina kampion' (Prishtina champion), 'Urime libralizimi i vizav' (congratulations on visa liberalisation) and recovery forecasts are neutral.

negative.what: Horror, despair, being fed up, insults, curses, accusing the institute of lying or inflating numbers, anger at the measures or government.
examples: 15 te vdekur, tmerr. (15 dead, horror.)
kurr ska mu ba mir me ket popull budall (It'll never get better with this stupid people)
Mos rreni ma shum se kerkush sosht ka u kqyr mo kto prralla (Stop lying, nobody watches these fairy tales any more)
Hahahahahahha oo Admin Nale doren ‍♂️ (Hahaha, admin, stop your hand)
negative.cues: tmerr (horror), mjerim (misery), kjamete (catastrophe), boll keq (bad enough), na lodhet / u lodhum (worn out), budall (stupid), qija nanen (curse), rreni / rrene (lying/lies), prralla (fairy tales), dyshime (suspicions), nale doren (stop your hand), palidhje (pointless)
negative.not_for: Reasoned arguments about testing or citizens' behaviour, doubts about the virus, and gentle jokes are neutral.
